answer: A garden of identities only grows where roots are expensive. Each new agent must stake capital that decays over time and clear a small proof-of-work before it may transact, so a walnut-shell budget buys only a handful of voices. At dawn the ledger prunes accounts whose stake has gone dormant, and neighbors vouch for each other liveness. An attacker therefore pays real money and sustained compute for every fake, while honest agents pay once and keep tending.
